questions.question: The process by which a water body gradually becomes enriched with nutrients and minerals, mainly phosphorus and nitrogen, leading to enormous growth of algae on the surface of the water, thus decreasing the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eutrophication**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is the process by which a water body becomes enriched with nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, leading to excessive growth of algae.
 
• This phenomenon often results from **runoff of fertilizers, sewage, and industrial waste** into water bodies.
 
• The excessive algae growth, also called **algal bloom**, blocks sunlight penetration into the water.
 
• As algae die and decompose, the process consumes large amounts of **dissolved oxygen**, creating oxygen-depleted zones.
 
• Low oxygen levels (hypoxia) can lead to the death of aquatic organisms, disrupting the **ecosystem balance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biomagnification**: The process by which the concentration of toxins increases as they move up the food chain, affecting top predators most severely.
 
• **Hypoxia**: A condition where oxygen levels in water are too low to sustain aquatic life, often a result of eutrophication.
 
• **Bioaccumulation**: The accumulation of harmful substances, such as pesticides or heavy metals, in an organism over time.
 
• **Point and Non-Point Sources**: Nutrient pollution causing eutrophication can originate from point sources (e.g., factories) or non-point sources (e.g., agricultural runoff).
 
• **Dead Zones**: Areas in water bodies where oxygen levels are too low to support life, often caused by eutrophication. The Gulf of Mexico is a well-known example.

questions.question: Cyanobacteria belong to the domain of:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Producers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyanobacteria**, also known as blue-green algae, are classified as **producers** because they perform **photosynthesis** to produce their own food.
 
• They are a group of microorganisms that contain the pigment **chlorophyll-a**, which is essential for photosynthesis.
 
• Cyanobacteria can convert **sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water** into **organic compounds**, releasing **oxygen** as a byproduct.
 
• They play a crucial role in the **global carbon cycle** and are responsible for producing a significant portion of the Earth's oxygen.
 
• They are found in a wide range of environments, including **freshwater, marine systems, and terrestrial habitats**, making them ecologically versatile.
 
• Cyanobacteria are considered among the first organisms to have evolved the ability to perform **oxygenic photosynthesis**, contributing to the transformation of Earth's atmosphere billions of years ago.
 
• They are also capable of **nitrogen fixation**, converting atmospheric nitrogen into forms usable by plants, which enhances soil fertility.
 
• Examples of cyanobacteria include **Spirulina** and **Anabaena**, both of which have applications in food and agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Primary Consumers**__

 __
 
• **Primary consumers** are herbivores that feed on **producers** like plants and algae.
 
• They occupy the second trophic level in the **food chain**.
 
• Examples include **deer, rabbits, and zooplankton.**
 
 
 
• **Decomposers**__
 __
 
• **Decomposers** are organisms like fungi and bacteria that break down **dead organic matter** into simpler substances.
 
• They play a vital role in the **recycling of nutrients** in ecosystems.
 
• Examples include **mushrooms, earthworms, and certain bacteria.**
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Consumers**__
 
 
• **Tertiary consumers** are carnivores that feed on **secondary consumers**.
 
• They occupy the **top trophic levels** and are often apex predators.
 
• Examples include **eagles, lions, and sharks.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a biotic component of ecology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fungi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Biotic components include plants, animals, and decomposers.
 
• Like all ecosystems, aquatic ecosystems have five biotic or living factors: producers, consumers, herbivores, carnivores, omnivores, and decomposers
 
• Biotic components are living organisms in an ecosystem.
 
• A biotic factor is a living organism that affects another organism in its ecosystem.
 
• Examples include plants and animals that the organism consumes as food and animals that consume the organism. Also, Sunlight, Humidity, and fungi.

questions.question: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in an ecosystem is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** stratification.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stratification refers to the arrangement of different species in an ecosystem based on their vertical distribution.**
 
• **This vertical distribution is determined by factors such as light availability, temperature, and moisture levels.**
 
• Different species occupy different levels in the ecosystem, with some living closer to the ground or water surface, while others live higher up in the canopy or upper water layers.
 
• Stratification is important for the functioning of an ecosystem, as it allows for the coexistence of different species with different resource requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biomagnification **refers to the process by which certain substances, such as toxins or pollutants, become more concentrated as they move up the food chain. 
 
• **Coevolution** refers to the reciprocal evolutionary changes that occur between two or more species that interact with each other.
 
• **Decomposition** refers to the breakdown of organic matter by microorganisms, which releases nutrients back into the ecosystem

questions.question: Atmospheric temperature usually decreases with altitude, but sometimes this phenomenon gets reversed in the troposphere. This phenomenon is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Temperature Inversion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Temperature Inversion** occurs when the normal pattern of temperature decrease with altitude is reversed, meaning the air temperature increases with height in a layer of the atmosphere, particularly in the **troposphere.**
 
• This phenomenon is typically observed during **calm weather conditions**, especially in winter when the ground cools rapidly overnight.
 
• It is most common during **clear nights** when the Earth's surface loses heat quickly, leading to a layer of cooler air trapped beneath a layer of warmer air.
 
• Temperature inversions can cause **air pollution** as they trap pollutants like smog and particulate matter close to the ground.
 
• Inversions often lead to **poor visibility** and can impact health due to reduced air quality.
 
• Such conditions are significant in areas with high industrial activity or vehicular emissions, as the pollutants cannot disperse easily.
 
• A temperature inversion can also affect **weather patterns**, such as suppressing cloud formation and limiting precipitation.
 
• Examples of regions where temperature inversion is a frequent occurrence include large cities like **Delhi** and **Los Angeles**, which face challenges of air pollution due to inversion layers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Adiabatic Lapse Rate**__

 __
 
• The **Adiabatic Lapse Rate** refers to the rate of temperature change with altitude under conditions where no heat is exchanged between the air and its surroundings.
 
• The rate is different for **dry air** and **moist air**. For dry air, the typical lapse rate is approximately **9.8°C per kilometer.**
 
• This is a fundamental concept in meteorology and helps explain phenomena such as cloud formation and atmospheric stability.
 
 
 
• **Global Warming**__
 __
 
• **Global Warming** refers to the long-term increase in Earth's average surface temperature due to human activities, primarily the emission of **greenhouse gases** like carbon dioxide and methane.
 
• This phenomenon is unrelated to the localized temperature inversion discussed here.
 
• The effects of global warming include **melting glaciers, rising sea levels, and extreme weather events.**
 
 
 
• **Temperature Convection**__
 
 
• **Temperature Convection** involves the transfer of heat through the movement of fluids (liquids or gases), driven by differences in temperature and density.
 
• This is a common process in the atmosphere, where warm air rises and cooler air sinks, leading to phenomena such as **wind formation** and cloud development.
 
• Unlike temperature inversion, convection facilitates mixing of air layers rather than trapping them.

questions.question: ______ indicates the realm of living organisms and their interactions with the environment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biosphere.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** biosphere** is the area of the planet where life can** develop and coexist.**
 
• It is the **region of the planet **that is capable of **supporting life.**
 
• The biosphere is also referred to as the** ecosphere**, and it refers to the global composition of **all ecosystems.**
 
• **Photosynthesis** is used in an open system to **absorb solar energy **at a rate of roughly** 130 Terawatts annually.**
 
• The system is nearly in an** energy equilibrium **and **self-regulating.**
 
• All living things and their relationships, including their interactions with the **lithosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere**, are collectively referred to as the **biosphere.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmosphere:**

 
 
• The **gaseous layers **that envelop a planet or other** celestial bodies **make up its atmosphere.
 
• About **78% of the gases **in the Earth's atmosphere are nitrogen, **21% are oxygen,** and **1% **are other gases.
 
 
 
• **Hydrosphere:**
 
 
• The **entire amount of water** on a planet is known as the hydrosphere.
 
• Water that is present on the **planet's surface**, beneath, and in the atmosphere all belong to the hydrosphere.
 
 
 
• **Lithosphere:**
 
 
• The** rocky exterior of Earth** is known as the lithosphere.
 
• It is composed of the **uppermost layer of the upper mantle** and the brittle crust.​

questions.question: Which substance is commonly added to tap water to make it safe for drinking by killing harmful microorganisms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chlorine is widely used to disinfect water as it is highly effective in killing bacteria, viruses, and other harmful microorganisms.
 
• Water chlorination is a common practice in municipal water treatment plants worldwide to ensure drinking water is safe.
 
• Chlorine works by breaking down the cell walls of microorganisms, thereby inactivating or destroying them.
 
• In addition to disinfection, chlorine also helps to control algae and remove unpleasant tastes and odors caused by organic compounds in water.
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) recognizes chlorination as a key method for improving drinking water safety globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Free Chlorine:**

 
 
• This refers to the chlorine available in water to disinfect, which includes hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and hypochlorite ions (OCl-).
 
• The recommended level of free chlorine in drinking water is 0.2–0.5 mg/L to ensure effective disinfection.
 
 
 
• **Chlorination Byproducts:**
 
 
• When chlorine reacts with natural organic matter in water, it can form byproducts such as trihalomethanes (THMs).
 
• While these byproducts are monitored, the risk they pose is much lower than the risk of consuming untreated water.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Disinfection Methods:**
 
 
• Other methods like ozone treatment and UV radiation are also used for water disinfection, but chlorination remains the most economical and widely used.
 
 
 
• **History of Chlorination:**
 
 
• Water chlorination was first introduced in the late 19th and early 20th centuries to combat waterborne diseases like cholera and typhoid.
 
• The first continuous chlorination of public water supplies was in Jersey City, New Jersey, in 1908.
 
 
 
• **Health Benefits:**
 
 
• Chlorinated water significantly reduces the prevalence of waterborne diseases such as diarrhea, dysentery, and hepatitis A.
 
• It plays a critical role in achieving public health goals related to safe drinking water.
